cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to all in Rome who are loved by God (Romans 1:1, 7). He just finished a big chain: those God called, He justified, and those He justified, He glorified (Romans 8:30). Now Paul stops and asks, "What then shall we say in response to these things?"

cards.question: Paul's next line starts with "If God is for us…" What does Paul say follows from that?

answers.text: No one can stand against us
Everyone will be on our side

cards.text: Then Paul points to the biggest gift there is. God "did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all."

cards.question: God already gave up His own Son for us all. So what does Paul say God will also do?

answers.text: Ask us to pay Him back
Hold back the rest for now

cards.text: Friend, if somebody hands you the keys to the WHOLE bakery, you don't stand there sweating about one sprinkle. Then Paul asks, "Who will bring any charge against God’s elect?"

cards.question: Who will bring any charge against God's elect? What answer does Paul give?

answers.text: Their good works speak for them

cards.text: Next question: "Who is there to condemn us?" Paul points to Christ Jesus, who died, was raised to life, and is at the right hand of God.

cards.question: Christ Jesus is at the right hand of God. What does Paul say He is doing there?

cards.text: Jesus, at God's right hand, in OUR corner. Me? Back in the junk drawer, the only ones in my corner were the dead batteries I shared it with. Friend, they couldn't even back up a TV remote.
Now Paul asks the big one: "Who shall separate us from the love of Christ?" And he lists trouble, distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger and sword.

cards.question: Paul lists trouble, distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger and sword. What kind of things are on that list?

cards.text: Then Paul quotes the Scriptures (Psalm 44:22): "For Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered." Heavy line, friend.

cards.question: True or false: after that whole list, Paul says trouble, famine or sword can separate us from the love of Christ.
In all those hard things, what does Paul say we are through Him who loved us?

cards.text: MORE than conquerors. Not "made it out." Not "survived with flour all over the apron." MORE. THAN. And it's through Him who loved us.
Then Paul says, "For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers," and he's not done yet.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the future might someday be able to separate us from God's love.
Paul adds height and depth. Then he covers everything else: nothing in all ___ will be able to separate us.
Paul ends by saying where this love of God is found. Where does he say it is?

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 3 quotes "did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This story card does not move the passage forward. It retells Romans 8:34 (Jesus at God's right hand, for us), which card 7 already told and card 8 already asked. It adds only a joke.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The story card runs to four sentences: "Jesus, at God's right hand, in OUR corner." / "Me?" / "Back in the junk drawer..." / "Friend, they couldn't...". Only the opening card may go past 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card is a recap of Romans 8:37 ("more than conquerors... through Him who loved us"), which card 14 just asked and answered. It does not carry the passage to a new moment.

The story card is about six sentences or fragments ("MORE than conquerors." / "Not 'made it out.'" / "Not 'survived...'" / "MORE." / "THAN." / "And it's through Him who loved us."). That is well over the limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says we are this "through Him who loved us". That wording rules out the wrong answer "Left to fight alone" before the baker reasons at all.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer "creation" is a whole category. The wrong answers "Israel" and "Rome" are single places, so they are not the same kind of thing. The question also says Paul "covers everything else", which rules out the two places on sight.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Seven of the ten choice cards are multiple choice. There are only two true or false cards and one fill in the blank, so multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
